items.title: 67247_J.C. Higginbotham oral history interview
items.q: So he came over and he begged my pardon, he really did. He said, "I'm sorry."

ctx.x: Anyway, I think I was at the restaurant counter. Jay had gone on an errand. So Sidney Catlett and I were sitting at the table and I ordered a sandwich and Jay came back.

We were getting ready to make the train back to New York. So Bill Robinson comes up to the place. There's this white fellow. He was high. Well, he, you know, knocked up against me. I didn't pay him no mind. So Bill Robinson said - you know we were youngsters then, very young. So he said, "Is this man molesting you?" Nobody had recognized Bill Robinson, so he's going to take it out on me to be recognized, and that's what I didn't like and neither did Sid Catlett. I said, "No, he's not molesting me. The man is just…

I said, "Why pick on me; I'm nobody." ... When Jay heard about it we had to quiet him down... "Why did you pick on Margaret to make yourself famous?" He was already famous; he didn't have to do that to me.
